subject: Finalizing MAP & commercial tradeoffs for Atlas Health - latency SLO tie-ins
messages:
From: Samantha Green <samantha.green@atlashealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Rajiv Patel <r.patel@atlashealth.com>
Date: 2026-01-10T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Atlas MAP / eval scope / SLA expectations

Karthik / Marissa —

Thanks for the call today. Quick recap from Atlas' side / asks as we build the MAP:
- We want a two-phase evaluation: a 2-week sandbox (functional) followed by a 30-day pilot with production traffic replay.
- Performance SLOs are critical for our UX team: 95th pct latency target for typical 512-token requests should be <200ms. If you can commit to tighter numbers at scale, that will influence the discount we can offer on a multi-quarter commit.
- We need milestones mapped to commercial concessions: what discount do we get after successful pilot? What ramp/commit is required to unlock it?
- Procurement wants a rough timeline (PO target) and an early draft SOW to start internal approvals.

Can you send a MAP draft that ties milestones to pricing/credits and a proposed SLO definition we can take to our SRE and procurement teams?

Samantha
Samantha Green
Director of Product, Atlas Health

Attachments: none

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Green <samantha.green@atlashealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rajiv Patel <r.patel@atlashealth.com>
Date: 2026-01-12T14:08:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Atlas MAP / eval scope / SLA expectations

Samantha —

Appreciate the clear asks. I've attached a first-pass MAP (MAP-Atlas-v2.pdf) and our latest latency benchmark summary (latency-benchmarks-20260108.csv). High level:

MAP highlights (summary):
- Phase 1: Sandbox validation (2 weeks) — functional pass, integration smoke tests, sample traffic. No commercial credit attached.
- Phase 2: Pilot (30 days) — production replay at agreed QPS. Success criteria = 95th pct latency < 150ms for the 512-token profile AND error rate < 0.5%.
- Commercial tie-ins:
  - If pilot meets success criteria within the 30-day window, Atlas can commit to a 6-month ramp with an initial reserved throughput (Tier 1) of 150K reqs/day. Unlocks 12% committed discount.
  - If Atlas extends to a 12-month commit at 300K reqs/day, additional 8% discount (20% total).
  - If the 95th pct latency exceeds 200ms for more than two non-consecutive days during the pilot, Redwood will provide a one-time service credit equal to 5% of monthly invoice for that month. If underperformance persists beyond 30 days, we propose an escalation path (engineering deep-dive + performance remediation window) in lieu of larger automatic credits.

We included a pricing matrix in the MAP and a draft SLO clause. Note: Rishi will circulate legal redlines for how SLOs and credits are codified in the contract.

Attachments: MAP-Atlas-v2.pdf, latency-benchmarks-20260108.csv

Next suggested steps:
1) Atlas reads MAP + benchmark.
2) Align on pilot QPS profile and exact request samples by Jan 15.
3) Redwood delivers SOW draft by Jan 16 so procurement can start review.

Happy to jump back on a call with SRE/procurement.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Samantha Green <samantha.green@atlashealth.com>, Rajiv Patel <r.patel@atlashealth.com>
Date: 2026-01-13T11:37:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Atlas MAP / eval scope / SLA expectations — legal redlines (draft)

Team / Samantha —

Quick legal/ops view on the MAP/SLO language Karthik shared. My top concerns:
- Ambiguity in "95th pct latency < 150ms" — we need to define request profile (payload size, tokenization), measurement windows (rolling 7-day vs calendar month), and whether client-side network latency is excluded. I recommend moving the SLO into an "SLA Exhibit" that defines metric, measurement method, and measurement endpoint.
- Credits calc: the MAP's proposed 5% one-time credit is acceptable as an initial concession, but we should add a cap (e.g., max 30% total credits over the first contract year) and require a remediation window to attempt fixes before credits auto-apply.
- Escalation: include a concrete cadence (48-hour initial response, 5 business-day mitigation plan) and an opt-out for Atlas if quality doesn't materially improve after remediation.
- Data/sample retention: Atlas asked for request profiles — we should include an agreed anonymization process and a retention schedule in the MAP.

Action items for Redwood:
1) I'll author a proposed SLA Exhibit and a credits table (examples of how many % credits at given breach durations).
2) Karthik/Marissa: confirm you can accept the measurement boundaries (rolling 7d) and remediation windows.

I'll circulate a redline by EOD.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Commercial Legal, Redwood Inference

From: Samantha Green <samantha.green@atlashealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Rajiv Patel <r.patel@atlashealth.com>, Procurement <procurement@atlashealth.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-01-15T08:23:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Atlas MAP / eval scope / SLA expectations — procurement notes

Thanks — quick notes from procurement/SRE after reviewing the MAP:
- Procurement: please provide a high-level SOW (we need deliverables, timeline, acceptance criteria) and a sample PO template if possible. Budget holder will make a decision once we see the SOW + pricing tiers.
- SRE: the 150ms target is attractive but asks for clarifications — are the numbers measured at the service edge or inferred from Redwood telemetry? We need to understand measurement endpoints (service-side vs client observations).
- Credits: procurement prefers automatic credits rather than a remediation-only approach for early-stage pilots. They asked if we can make credits tiered (e.g., 5% credit for single-day breach, 15% for sustained breach >7 days).

Procurement contact: procurement@atlashealth.com (looped).

Can the Redwood team provide: SOW draft + explicit SLA Exhibit showing measurement methods + updated credits table by Jan 19? That will let us schedule an internal review the week of Jan 20.

Thanks,
Samantha

Subject: Re: Atlas MAP / eval scope / SLA expectations — final draft & next steps

Samantha / Rajiv / team —

Thanks for the feedback. Attached: SOW-Atlas-v1.docx and an updated MAP with an SLA Exhibit and credits table. Summary of changes and commitments:

1) Measurement & exhibit:
- SLO defined for the 512-token profile, measured at Redwood's service edge and reported in rolling 7-day windows. Client-side noise excluded. We include an instrumentation plan so Atlas SRE can validate telemetry.

2) Credits & caps:
- Tiered credits: single-day breach = 5% credit for that month; sustained breach (>7 consecutive days) = 15% credit for each affected month. Credits capped at 30% in any 12-month period.
- Credits become payable after a 5-business-day remediation period; if Atlas elects to terminate after sustained breach, we include an exit assistance clause.

3) Commercial milestones & discounts:
- Pilot success (95th <150ms & error rate <0.5%) -> Atlas signs a 6-month reserved commitment (Tier 1: 150K reqs/day) -> 12% committed discount applied starting month 1 after PO.
- If Atlas commits to 12 months @ 300K reqs/day within 60 days of pilot completion -> additional 8% (20% total).
- If at onboarding Redwood needs to request extra ramp capacity for peak forecasts, we will provide a 30-day notice and temporary burst pricing; this does not affect the committed discount unless sustained over 60 days.

4) Timeline / next steps:
- Redwood delivers final SOW & MAP (attached) — today (Jan 19).
- Atlas to confirm pilot QPS profile and sign MAP by Jan 23 to keep the target PO by Feb 2.
- Redwood to run a brief performance onboarding with Atlas SREs the week of Jan 26 (we'll book 2 x 90-min sessions).

Attachments: SOW-Atlas-v1.docx, MAP-Atlas-v2.pdf, latency-benchmarks-20260108.csv

If these terms look good, please confirm and we'll raise the standard order form. Happy to take one more call with procurement on Thursday.

Best,
—Karthik

Account Executive, Redwood Inference
